paragraphs: It is argued that school should reward students who show the best academic results; some others, however, believe that students who have improvements should be rewarded. Basic from my perspective, There are some cases to be made for both sides of the arguments.

Admittedly, students who show the best academic results need to be given an award to their efforts. Students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, deserving their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards. Therefore, they can propel towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition has seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face on fierce competition and enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who have an effort in study should be rewarded. Only a few smart students can come first and receive the remunerative. That cause others to think that their effort is futile because they cannot surpass those understanding individuals and prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. Likewise, emphasizing improvements encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constantly desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination.

paragraphs: Some people believe that schools should reward students who achieve the best academic results, whereas others think that it is more important to reward students who show progress. From my perspective, schools should reward both groups.

Admittedly, students who achieve the best academic results deserve rewards for their efforts. Since they have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage them and other students to study harder, which may lead to overall academic gains. Furthermore, competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Becoming familiar with this reality can help students thrive in the face of fierce competition and may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, other students may feel that further effort is futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and may lose the incentive to study. By contrast, recognizing improvement can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and can help them understand that they need to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. The constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit students more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, schools should reward both students who achieve the best academic results and those who make progress. In this way, schools recognize both high achievement and efforts to improve.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary as computers make historical objects and works of art available online. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought: digital access cannot replace visits to these places.

Admittedly, technology provides useful access to culture and history. Firstly, high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms make it easier for people to explore artworks and artefacts in detail without leaving home. For example, a virtual tour of Louvre museum could let viewers study artworks from home. This is especially useful for people who cannot afford to travel or have mobility issues, as they can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, public museums and art galleries are still necessary. Even as three-dimensional technology develops rapidly, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Such a visit can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, seeing a historical artefact up close may make its age and authenticity more vivid than a screen image can. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. This role can draw tourists and bring members of a community together.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that public museums and art galleries will remain necessary. These venues provide direct experiences and community value that computers cannot replace.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that Dangerous sports should be prohibited by law. Meanwhile, Some individuals argue that it should be free to take part. I am personally of the latter school of though provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous Sports should be prohibited. Due to even a minor error made by player, can result in participant's death. An example is sky diving. However, I think this ban is unfeasible, The reason is remote locations, say mountain cliffs, monitoring is minimal surveillance. On the other hand, a police officer follows every individual can be unrealistic. Therefore, a prohibition exists only on paper. Thereby, causing a situation that people driving practice underground and harder to ensure basic safety standards

Personally, People should be to permitted to do any sport as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. People can attend reputable club, for example are deep-ocean diving, bungee jumping, thereby gaining access to appropriate equipments and qualify supervision. However, [chưa đọc rõ] amateur need to be accompanied by an expert and be taught what to do when accident occur to recognize dangers. Nevertheless, it is necessary to have a proper training and necessary precautions.
In conclusion, banning neither practical nor effective. People have freedom to chose, under strict conditions of training. That is a more realistic approach

Body 2 thêm 'to' vào 'be to permitted' và không giải thích huấn luyện giảm rủi ro thế nào. Em phải viết lại cả bài, tự dựng câu có chủ–vị, dùng từ nối theo quan hệ thật và bổ sung bước huấn luyện → giảm rủi ro; Cô không quy lỗi cho đoạn chữ chồng chưa đọc chắc.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited. Even a minor error made by a player can result in a participant's death. An example is sky diving. However, I think this ban is unfeasible. The first reason is that these sports occur in remote locations, say mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. Furthermore, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow every individual. Therefore, a prohibition exists only on paper. This may drive the practice underground, making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

Personally, people should be permitted to do any sport as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. People can register with a reputable club for sports such as deep-ocean diving and bungee jumping, thereby gaining access to appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. However, beginners still need to be accompanied by an expert and be taught what to do when accidents occur to recognise dangers. Therefore, proper training and necessary precautions can make participation safer, although no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, banning is neither practical nor effective. People have the freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness. That is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: There is an argument that children should have the freedom to learn through trial and error. Meanwhile, others think adults need to help them avoid mistakes. From my perspective, children should be allowed to make mistakes, provided that those errors do not involve serious danger.

On the one hand, those who want adults to prevent mistakes emphasize the harm mistakes can cause. Children do not need to get hurt by knives, fire or electricity to learn to be careful. Moreover, parents who pre-emptively help children can have peace of mind since they know they have done their best to protect and raise them.

Those on the other side have their own valid reasoning. Parents cannot be around children all the time; therefore, children need to experiment with new things and some mistakes are inevitable. Furthermore, children can learn invaluable lessons from these errors, and those lessons may stand them in good stead later in life. Children who are shielded from everything may grow up overdependent on others, an undesirable trait.

Overall, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes is a good way to prepare them for the future, provided that parents give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail that future.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares carbon emissions from gas, oil and coal in the UK between 1990 and 2010. The figures are measured in millions of tons.

Overall, emissions from gas increased throughout the period and became the highest from 2000 onwards. Coal emissions declined steadily, while oil emissions fell overall, although they rose briefly between 1995 and 2000.

In 1990, coal caused approximately 310 million tons of emissions, the highest of the three. Oil accounted for about 270 million tons, followed by gas at around 220 million tons. Five years later, gas had risen to roughly 270 million tons, almost catching coal at around 280 million tons. Oil, meanwhile, had fallen to about 240 million tons. By 2000, gas reached 300 million tons and overtook both remaining sources.

From 2000 to 2010, gas emissions rose further from 300 to approximately 320 million tons. In contrast, coal emissions dropped from about 250 to 190 million tons, making coal the smallest source at the end. Oil fell from around 260 million tons in 2000 to 210 million tons in 2010, despite its earlier temporary rise.

criteria.comment: Em nêu được hai luồng ý kiến và nói cả hai có lợi ích, nhưng bài dừng ngay sau “history can teach students”. Chưa có lời giải thích cho lợi ích lịch sử, chưa có đoạn khoa học và chưa có kết luận, nên yêu cầu thảo luận cả hai phía chưa được thực hiện.

criteria.label: CC
criteria.comment: Có một mở bài và dấu hiệu mở thân bài, dùng “On the one hand” đúng vị trí dự kiến. Bài dừng giữa câu nên chưa thể hiện được sự phát triển và liên kết các đoạn.

criteria.label: LR
criteria.comment: Có vài từ đúng chủ đề như history, science, technology, nhưng “an argue”, “beneficiary”, “nowaday” dùng sai; phạm vi từ quan sát được còn hẹp.

criteria.label: GRA
criteria.comment: Một số cấu trúc cơ bản vẫn hiểu được, nhưng lỗi loại từ, hòa hợp và mạo từ xuất hiện ngay trong phần ngắn đã viết.

paragraphs.text: Some people consider history one of the most important school subjects, whereas others believe that science and technology deserve greater attention in the modern world. I think both areas offer benefits that students need, although those benefits are different.

History can teach students how past events shaped the society in which they live. By examining important decisions and conflicts, they can understand why their country developed certain institutions and traditions. For example, studying a struggle for independence can help young people appreciate the sacrifices of earlier generations and develop a stronger connection to their community. History also asks students to compare accounts and consider the evidence behind them. These skills can make them more careful when judging claims about present-day events.

Science and technology, on the other hand, prepare students for practical challenges and a changing workplace. Science lessons help them test ideas and solve problems by using evidence. Technology classes can give them experience with digital tools that many jobs require. For example, a student who learns basic programming may later help develop software for hospitals, schools or transport. Scientific knowledge can also support research into pollution and disease. These subjects therefore open career options and allow future workers to contribute to society in ways that historical knowledge alone may not.

In conclusion, history helps young people understand the past and their place in society, while science and technology equip them to address modern problems. Schools should give students a solid foundation in both fields rather than allowing one to replace the other.
